title: Service as worship
hookLine: God says, I was sick and you did not visit Me: how could God be sick?
tomorrow: do you have to be an expert before you share?

lines: I WAS SICK, AND YOU DID NOT VISIT ME.
cards: Service hours. A form, a supervisor's signature, a number for an application. Some service gets logged.
Some never does. In a hadith in Sahih Muslim, God speaks, and keeps the log in the oddest way. On the Day of Judgment, God says: O son of Adam, I was sick and you did not visit Me.
The man is baffled. How could I visit You, when You are the Lord of the worlds? Fair question.

teach.b: God's answer solves it. My servant so-and-so was sick, and you did not visit him.

teach.h: YOU'D HAVE FOUND ME WITH HIM.
teach.b: Didn't you know that if you had visited him, you would have found Me with him? Then twice more. I asked you for food and you didn't feed Me.
I asked you for water and you gave Me none. Each time the same answer: had you fed him, had you given him drink, you would have found that with Me. So God isn't sick.
God is with the sick. The visit you skipped was a visit you could have made to Him. That's inside today's line: service with the right intention is prayer in action.
The hadith that opens Sahih al-Bukhari says it plainly: actions are only by intentions, and each person gets what they intended.
Two people carry the same box of groceries to a neighbor. For one, it's hours for a form. For the other, it's also a visit to someone God is with.
The box weighs the same. What it is depends on why. This isn't a rule against logging hours.
Some Muslims say a quiet bismillah, in the name of God, before a task, which turns an errand toward worship without changing the errand at all.

how: Muslims speak of setting the intention (niyyah) before good work, and some say bismillah before a task; visiting the sick, feeding people and giving water are counted as worship when done for God's sake.

o: praying for people instead of helping them
working full time for a mosque or charity
helping people for God's sake, as worship

games.q: what's inside the puzzle — tap the pairs.
p: you'd have found Me with him
you'd have found that with Me

s: in the hadith, God says He was actually sick
God is with the sick: 'you would have found Me with him.'
in Islam, worship only means the ritual prayer
service done for God's sake counts as worship too; God is with the one you visit.
the hadith that opens Sahih al-Bukhari says actions are by intentions
and each person gets what they intended.

games.q: you're taking soup to a sick roommate and you're annoyed about it the whole way there. is it still worth bringing?
o: bring it, and turn the why on the way: God is with the sick, the hadith says.
skip it; if your heart isn't in it, the act counts for nothing at all.
bring it, but it's only a favor; worship is what happens on a prayer mat.
games.why: God says: had you visited him, you would have found Me with him. the act is right, and the intention can be turned on the way.

practice: Close your eyes and bring to mind one ordinary task waiting for you today: dishes, an email, a shift. Hold it there without changing it, and ask quietly what it would become if you did it for God's sake, or for the person it helps.
Stay with that answer until the time is up.

wordCard.voice: Service as worship: helping people with the right intention, so the help itself becomes prayer. In the hadith, God is with the sick.

orig.note: Arabic: intention, what you mean by an act. actions are only by intentions.

carryVoice: Your line: service is prayer. Same box of groceries, carried with a different why. Peace for now.

sources.ref: Sahih Muslim 2569 (hadith qudsi): O son of Adam, I was sick and you did not visit Me... had you visited him you would have found Me with him; likewise food and drink
Sahih al-Bukhari 1: actions are only by intentions, and each person will have what he intended
